issues.body: Both ownership probes pass `is_human=lambda login: login.casefold() == args.maintainer.casefold()`. `label_application_machine_owned` defines every non-App label event whose actor fails that probe as machine-owned. Consequently, a direct `review:needs-user` or source `needs:user` application by any human maintainer/collaborator other than the single configured login authorizes this sweep to clear the hold. The workflow does not supply `--maintainer`, so the only recognized human is the default `jeswr`, including on `sparq-org` targets. This contradicts the receipt's promise that a human can reapply the label and no automation may override it, and opens an automatic transition based on author identity without a real permission/association check.
issues.fix_hint: Use the repository's strict collaborator-permission human probe (the same permission-based predicate used by the existing worker flow) for every timeline actor, with lookup failures resolving to human-owned/not-clearable. Add entry-point tests with a non-default authorized human applying each of the PR and issue holds and assert that no comment or label write occurs; keep separate bot/App-driven controls proving the machine-owned path remains reachable.
issues.title: Human holds from every maintainer except one are treated as machine-owned

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The two prior operational findings are materially addressed: population payloads are validated, write failures are distinguished and fatal, all-row operational failure exits nonzero, and the workflow consumes those statuses. However, the new automatic-unpark path does not actually prove that the label actor was non-human. It recognizes only one configured login as human, so a label applied directly by any other human maintainer/collaborator is classified as machine-owned and may be removed. Because this is a new major trust-boundary finding in round 2, progress is regressing under the required scale.
